question.text: A derivative is a financial product whose value is:

answer.text: Derived from the value of another product called the underlying
Fixed at the time of contract creation and does not change
Determined independently without reference to any other asset
Set by the government based on economic conditions

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 195, a derivative is a financial product whose value is derived from another product called the underlying. Pages 196-197 reinforce this link to the underlying and give examples (equity, index, currency, interest rate, commodities). The Trap: Option B contradicts the source — derivative values move with the underlying. Option C also contradicts the source — value is by definition derived from another asset. Option D is unsupported; the source does not describe derivative values as being set by government. Note: The underlying can include gold, equity shares, an index, a currency, an interest rate, or other assets whose values change over time.
